blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Large-scale robotic simulation requires diverse deformable objects with executable physical properties and realistic interaction behaviors. However, existing 3D asset collections primarily emphasize visual diversity, while scalable physical construction and verification remain challenging. We introduce RFW-S, a large-scale dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified assets spanning 485 everyday categories across five structural families: soft solids, cloth sheets, shells, garments, and bags. We develop an automated pipeline integrating reference-guided 3D generation, structure-aware physical modeling, and LLM-assisted parameter estimation and calibration. To ensure physical reliability, we introduce an independent simulation verification framework that evaluates object behaviors under interactions distinct from those used for parameter calibration. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of independent verification and characterize deformable responses under different physical configurations. We further evaluate robotic grasping in terms of both task success and object integrity, and demonstrate the physical realism of our simulated objects through sim-to-real replay of fragile-object manipulation. RFW-S provides a scalable foundation for physically grounded simulation and embodied robotic learning.
blocks.zh: 大规模机器人模拟需要具有可执行物理属性和现实互动行为的多样性可变形物体. 然而,现有的三维资产收藏主要强调视觉多样性,而可扩展的实体构造和核查仍然具有挑战性。 我们引入了RFW-S, 一个由83,365个模拟验证资产组成的大规模数据集, 跨越了485个日常类别, 跨越了五个结构家庭:软固体、布单、贝壳、服装和袋子。 我们开发了一个自动管道,将参考制导的3D生成、结构感知的物理模型以及LLM辅助参数估计和校正结合起来。 为确保物理可靠性,我们引入了一个独立的模拟核查框架,用以评价相互作用下与参数校正所使用的相互作用下的对象行为。 广泛的实验表明独立核查的有效性,并描述不同物理结构下可变形的反应。 我们进一步从任务成功和物体完整性的角度评价机器人的把握,并通过对脆弱物体操纵的模拟回放来展示模拟物体的物理现实主义. RFW-S为物理基础模拟提供了可扩展的基础并体现了机器人学习.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Robots operating in everyday environments must interact with objects whose
shape changes under contact: a sponge compresses during grasping, a towel
drapes over a surface, and a bag folds as it is lifted. These responses
affect how contact is established, whether a grasp succeeds, and whether an
object remains intact. Simulation offers a way to study such interactions
across object types and physical conditions, but doing so requires a diverse
collection of deformable assets with executable, tested physical behavior.

blocks.en:
Existing resources provide important parts of this foundation. Large 3D
collections offer broad visual diversity [ 1 ] , while
clothing datasets and deformable simulation environments provide specialized
geometry and interaction settings [ 2 , 3 ] . Recent systems further connect
asset construction to physics: ManiTwin verifies rigid-object grasps,
PhysX-Omni generates assets across physical types, and Agentic Real2Sim
reconstructs recorded interaction episodes [ 4 , 5 , 6 ] .
For everyday deformables, the remaining challenge is to combine broad
semantic coverage with physical configurations that can be reused and
assessed beyond the interactions used to construct them.

blocks.en:
This challenge extends beyond assigning material parameters to a generated
mesh. Deformation depends jointly on geometry, structural constraints,
material controls, and contact. A filled soft object needs interior
material, an open bag needs a preserved cavity and opening, and a garment
needs a surface representation that permits folding. An unsuitable
representation can prevent the intended response even when its material
parameters are adjusted. Moreover, a configuration that runs without
numerical failure may still deform incorrectly, and one that satisfies a
calibration interaction may fail under a different stimulus. Scaling asset
generation, therefore, requires both structure-aware physical construction
and behavioral evaluation that is separate from candidate selection.

blocks.en:
We introduce RoboFlyWheel-Soft (RFW-S) , a resource of 83,365 simulation-verified assets spanning 485 everyday categories across five structural families: soft solids, cloth sheets, shells,
garments, and bags (Figure 1 ). We construct a category-balanced
pool of 100,000 assets through reference-guided generation, adapt their
geometry to compatible simulation representations, and use a multimodal
language model to estimate effective physical parameters. Simulation
feedback guides bounded corrections to supported controls. Each asset links its executed configuration to recorded behavioral evidence.

blocks.en:
The central design is to separate calibration from final verification.
Once calibration selects a candidate, we freeze its geometry,
representation, parameters, and numerical settings, then evaluate it with
a distinct interaction. A separately scheduled
runtime and behavioral contract check evaluates execution, finite state,
and response criteria under a drop probe. In total, 83,365 assets pass both physical verification and the runtime and behavioral contract check, spanning all 485 everyday object categories.

blocks.en: We evaluate RFW-S through controlled physical tests, robotic grasping, and sim-to-real experiments. Our results show that material tuning alone cannot replace structural adaptation, and that calibration success does not guarantee valid behavior under a different interaction, motivating independent verification. Grasping experiments expose the gap between task completion and object integrity. Finally, replaying simulated gripper closure commands on a real robot reproduces both breakage and intact transfer, supporting the physical realism of our fragile-object simulation.
blocks.zh: 我们通过有控制的物理测试、机器人抓取 以及模拟到现实的实验来评估RFW-S。 我们的结果表明,仅靠材料调整不能取代结构调整,而校准成功并不能保证在不同的相互作用下采取有效的行为,激励独立核查。 格拉斯平实验暴露了任务完成和物体完整性之间的差距. 最后,在真正的机器人上重播模拟的抓取器关闭命令,既复制破损又完整地转移,支持我们脆弱的物体模拟的物理现实主义.

blocks.en:
Our contributions are threefold: • A large-scale dataset of everyday deformable objects. RFW-S provides 83,365 simulation-verified assets spanning 485 categories and
five structural families, with executable physical configurations and
associated behavioral evidence. • A scalable pipeline for physically verified asset construction. We combine structure-aware modeling, language-model-assisted parameter
estimation, and simulation-guided calibration with independent interaction
tests that screen for failures beyond calibration. • Physical and downstream validation. Controlled studies demonstrate the importance of structural adaptation and
independent verification. Robotic grasping evaluates task success alongside
object integrity, while sim-to-real replay reproduces both breakage and
intact transfer, supporting the realism of fragile-object simulation.

blocks.en: 6.3 Task completion and the integrity readout
blocks.zh: 第6.3条 任务完成和完整性读出

blocks.en:
The grasping application reports task completion together with a specified
integrity criterion. Every reported outcome exceeds the proxy threshold,
limiting comparisons based on binary intact success. The deformation-gradient
readout also responds to rigid rotation. A rotation-invariant strain measure
and calibration against physical damage observations would strengthen its
physical interpretation. Such a change would require recomputing the scores
and outcomes. The sim-to-real replay complements this proxy with a physical
observation: the gripper closure that crushes tofu in simulation crushes the
real tofu, and the non-damaging closure transfers it intact in both domains.
This agreement supports the physical realism of the simulated assets for
fragile manipulation. Paired force and deformation measurements on the
physical robot would further quantify response fidelity across materials.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
RFW-S connects 100,000 generated assets in 485 everyday deformable categories
to structure-compatible representations, effective parameters, and recorded
behavioral evidence. Physical verification and the separately scheduled RC check
jointly retain 83,365 assets and all categories. Independent testing exposes
calibration-accepted response mismatches, while configuration comparisons
and a grasping application distinguish deformation, task completion, and
a specified integrity criterion. The resulting resource supports reproducible
deformable-object studies with explicit configuration and evaluation scope.
Broader stimuli and paired physical measurements can extend that evidence
toward new interactions and real-object fidelity.

blocks.en:
A local diagnostic study tests three soft solids and a cloth sheet (Figure 14 ). The

the response; for example, the first solid’s tail-to-peak speed ratio changes
from 0.147 to 0.008 at the tested lower yield stress. The response is
object-dependent: the second solid remains near the 0.05 diagnostic boundary.
This motivates identifying effective solver controls before using a semantic
parameter proposal as a correction direction.

from an unsupported material response.

blocks.en:
A natural extension of RFW-S is toward hybrid articulated–deformable
objects, where rigid kinematic structures are coupled with soft components
such as fabric covers, straps, cushions, seals, membranes, or compliant
connectors. Extending the current structure-aware construction and independent
verification procedure to such mixed systems could bridge deformable-object
simulation with articulated reconstruction, part-level kinematics, and
physically grounded interaction [ 33 , 34 , 35 , 36 , 37 , 5 , 38 , 39 ] .

blocks.en:
At the scene level, RFW-S assets could serve as physically grounded building
blocks for generative simulation. Future systems could automatically compose
editable and executable worlds with scene layouts, lighting, articulated and
deformable objects, and task-relevant interactions, supporting scalable data
generation as well as controlled construction of rare or challenging scenarios [ 40 , 41 , 42 , 43 , 44 , 45 , 46 , 47 , 48 ] .

blocks.en:
Beyond explicit simulation, the physical configurations and executed
interaction traces in RFW-S could support 4D and physics-aware video
generation. Coupling simulator states with generative video renderers could
provide controllable dynamics under object motion, camera trajectories,
illumination, and external interactions, while video-to-4D reconstruction
could close the loop by recovering structured, simulation-ready worlds from
real or generated observations [ 49 , 50 , 51 , 48 , 52 ] .

blocks.en:
Finally, RFW-S could support broader embodied benchmarks and policy learning
beyond the grasp–lift–hold protocol studied here, including long-horizon
deformable manipulation, bimanual and high-DoF dexterity, VLA training,
safety-aware interaction, and sim-to-real evaluation. Its physical
verification and integrity records could enable evaluation criteria that
jointly consider task completion, object preservation, and physical or
semantic safety [ 3 , 14 , 53 , 54 , 55 , 56 , 57 , 58 , 59 , 60 , 61 ] .
